review_candidates.description: Director of Solar Water Farm Development & Deployment Location: Remote | Reports to: VP of Solar Water Farms | Department: Solar Water Farms WHO WE ARE GivePower's mission is to electrify the world with clean energy and provide greater health, economic, and educational opportunities to those who need them most. Since 2013, we've constructed nearly 2,800 solar projects across 33 countries, improving the lives of over 3 million people. Our growing team is made up of passionate, creative problem-solvers who value community, vision, and impact. If you crave an opportunity to meaningfully improve the lives of those in need, come join the charge. JOB SUMMARY The Director of SWF Development & Deployment manages and oversees GivePower’s Solar Water Farm (SWF) projects globally, from early-stage development through construction and handover to operations. Reporting to the VP of Solar Water Farms, this leader leads the planning, execution, and delivery of a portfolio of projects while working closely with internal teams, contractors, vendors, and partners to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to quality standards. Working closely with the VP of Solar Water Farms, the Director translates the program’s expansion goals into executable project plans. A key emphasis is leading the project team and owning scope, schedule, budget, and contractor performance for every Solar Water Farm leading up to site launch. The role contributes greatly to the level of GivePower’s impact firsthand and is an instrumental part of creating sustainable solutions to one of the world’s most pressing challenges. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Site Development: Oversees all aspects of the SWF site development process, including project identification, market research, and technical validation, and presents projects to senior leadership for go/no-go decisions. Land, Permitting & Approvals: Oversees land acquisition, permitting, and early-stage approvals with legal, project developers, government authorities, and local stakeholders. Market Validation: Collaborates with Country Managers to assess market validation, project risks, and alignment with organizational goals. Feasibility & Scoping: Works with engineering and deployment teams to assess technical and financial feasibility and define scope, schedule, and budget for each project. Construction Oversight: Oversees SWF construction, including contractor site safety, quality, and environmental compliance. Bidding & Contractor Selection: Leads local RFP and bid processes, including bid package preparation, bid analysis, and contractor negotiations, and recommends contractor selection to the VP of Solar Water Farms. Contracts & Project Documentation: Oversees project mechanics and documentation, including contracts, invoices, change orders, and payment milestones, approving within delegated authority and escalating as needed. Handover to Operations: Oversees the transition from Deployment to Operations, including site opening planning and budget, coordination between deployment, O&M, and site operations teams, internal handover documentation, and closeout documentation required by authorities for operation and distribution of water. KPIs & Reporting: Tracks progress against KPIs and reports on project status to senior leadership and stakeholders. review_candidates.description: The Opportunity Network (OppNet) Since 2003, The Opportunity Network (OppNet) has been committed to providing students, regardless of background, with the resources and connections necessary to achieve their college and career goals. OppNet's founding Fellows program supports 1,000 New York City students each year, from the summer after tenth grade through college graduation, with a 98% graduation rate within six years. About 93% of Fellows are first-generation college students, and 91% secure meaningful employment or graduate school admission within six months of graduating. OppNet extends this impact nationally through its Career Fluency® Partnerships program, which strengthens workforce and college readiness for 100,000 students across 20 cities, and through Opportunity Ignited, which helps employers improve talent pipelines and workplace environments and has trained more than 350 staff at 22 partner firms in its first five years. The Opportunity This is a rare opportunity to lead the people function at a moment when the right leader will shape what comes next. OppNet is entering a new chapter: a new CEO is expected to join in early 2027. The Director of People and Culture will step in at a time when people leadership has immediate, visible impact, helping to welcome and integrate a new CEO, guiding staff through change, and building the practices and culture that will carry OppNet forward. Throughout this transition, OppNet remains focused on doing its core work exceptionally well, and the Director will be central to making that possible.OppNet aims to practice internally what it advocates for externally: to be the kind of workplace it hopes its young people will one day join. That commitment shows up in an asset-based approach to people leadership that starts from employees' strengths and keeps their individual needs at the center of every policy and decision. OppNet is seeking a hands-on people leader who brings both heart and operational rigor to this moment. The Director of People and Culture will serve as the organization's senior HR practitioner, leading day-to-day people operations while guiding staff and managers through change, carrying OppNet's culture and values forward, and building a strong people foundation for the organization's next chapter under new leadership. The Director will play a key role in supporting the incoming CEO's transition and integration with staff, and will supervise the Senior Coordinator of People and Culture. Key Responsibilities The Director of People and Culture will lead OppNet's people operations, culture, and employee experience. The percentages below are estimates of how the Director's time will be divided across core areas of responsibility. Each area will remain central to the role, though their relative weight may shift as People & Culture priorities evolve. Responsibilities include: Change Management & Organizational Transition (20%) Partner with the Senior Director of Strategic Initiatives & Impact and the leadership team to plan and implement the people-related aspects of organizational change, including the onboarding and integration of the incoming CEO Develop and carry out change management plans, supporting clear, timely, and transparent communication with staff about organizational shifts Serve as a trusted resource for staff during transition, surfacing concerns, monitoring morale and engagement, and recommending responses to leadership Equip managers with the tools and coaching needed to lead their teams through change Adapt people policies, practices, and structures as organizational priorities evolve, with attention to sustainability and available resources HR Operations, Compliance & Systems (20%) Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations Oversee benefits administration and leave management, and help staff understand and make full use of OppNet's benefits Partner with Finance on payroll and manage the People and Culture budget, including cost tracking, forecasting, and annual budgeting Maintain and update the employee handbook and people policies Manage and strengthen OppNet's people systems, including the HRIS (ADP Workforce Now) and applicant tracking system In partnership with the Senior Director of Strategic Initiatives & Impact, maintain OppNet's compensation approach and recommend adjustments to ensure pay is competitive, fair, and equitable Talent, Performance & Development (20%) Manage the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, performance management, retention, and offboarding Lead structured, equitable hiring processes in partnership with hiring managers, aligned with the core competencies for each role Design orientation and onboarding experiences that work well for a remote and hybrid workforce Support managers in using performance management systems to create strong individual development plans, and identify professional development opportunities responsive to individual and organizational needs In time, and in partnership with leadership, spearhead the creation and implementation of a learning and development program to support professional development across the organization Conduct exit interviews and use retention and exit data to inform improvements Culture, Engagement & Team Leadership (25%) Design and administer staff engagement and culture surveys, analyze results, and create opportunities for staff and teams to process findings and set priorities Manage employee relations, ensuring staff concerns are addressed promptly, fairly, and confidentially Coach and advise managers and leaders on HR best practices and effective management Facilitate learning and dialogue around inclusion, psychological safety, and leadership accountability Supervise, coach, and develop the Senior Coordinator of People and Culture Organizational Learning, Development, and Program Reflection (15%) Participate in organization-wide learning sessions, working groups, and optional affinity groups. Shape and attend All-Hands meetings (~monthly) and State of OppNet meetings (~quarterly), and shape and attend weekly team meetings, periodic team retreats, and annual institution-wide retreats. Qualifications We take a broad view of experience and welcome applicants whose paths do not follow a traditional trajectory. The successful candidate will be genuinely motivated by OppNet's mission and will see people operations as a powerful way to advance social impact. The strongest candidates will bring: Eight or more years of progressive experience in HR, people operations, or organizational development, including at least three years leading an HR function managing people or comparable scope and ownership, even without the formal title A track record of guiding organizations through change, such as leadership transitions or fluctuations in resources, ideally in a mission-driven or nonprofit setting Broad HR generalist expertise and an enthusiasm for hands-on work across all areas of the function, including benefits administration, payroll, employee relations, and compliance Strong knowledge of employment law and HR compliance, including New York State and City requirements Previous experience managing workforces across multiple states of residence Exceptional interpersonal, facilitation, and conflict-resolution skills, with a demonstrated ability to build trust and influence across all levels of an organization Experience building effective talent systems, including recruitment, onboarding, professional development, and performance management A strength for developing HR processes and tools that improve efficiency, transparency, and accountability An asset-based, employee-centered approach to people leadership Experience fostering connection and belonging within a remote or distributed workforce Sound judgment, discretion, and integrity in handling sensitive and confidential information Experience with an HRIS (ADP Workforce Now preferred) Position Specifications This is a full-time, exempt position.
